lesson.title: Wechselpräpositionen Sentence Gym
lesson.subtitle: Twenty picture-prompt sentences switching cases by motion vs location

hook.title: The Gym at Full Weight
hook.content: No more pairs — full sentences at speed. Each prompt is a scene: is anything moving across a boundary? Accusative. Is everything at rest? Dative. Ich stelle das Glas auf den Tisch (I put the glass onto the table — motion). Das Glas steht auf dem Tisch (the glass stands on the table — rest). Same glass, same table, two cases — and the verb is the tell: stellen (put) moves, stehen (stand) rests. Twenty reps, and the wechsel (switch) becomes reflex.

footnotes.title: The Verb Is the Tell
footnotes.content: When unsure, check the verb: motion verbs (gehen, fahren, kommen, stellen, legen, hängen-onto, setzen) demand accusative after two-way prepositions. Rest verbs (sein, stehen, liegen, sitzen, hängen-rest) demand dative. The preposition only borrows the verb's case.

pattern.title: The Twenty Reps, Compressed
pattern.content: Ich gehe in die Stadt / Ich bin in der Stadt. Wir fahren in die Berge? hint — Berge (mountains). Das Glas steht auf dem Tisch / Ich stelle das Glas auf den Tisch. Die Katze springt auf den Tisch / Die Katze schläft auf dem Sofa? hint — sofa. Vor das Haus (driving up to it) / vor dem Haus (parked). Hinter den Baum? hint — Baum (tree) / hinter dem Baum. Neben den Tisch / neben dem Tisch. Über die Straße (crossing) / über dem Haus (hovering). Setz dich? hint — setzen (sit-put) neben mich / Ich sitze neben dir — sitzen takes the DATIVE OF PERSON: sitz NEXT TO ME = setz dich neben mich, accusative mich for the moved body, dative dir for the location-frame. The gym is complete.
pattern.linguist_note: sich setzen (sit down) vs sitzen (be seated) is the motion/rest pair hidden inside reflexives — setzen moves the body (accusative: sich), sitzen describes the body at rest (location → dative frame). English 'sit/set' made the same distinction once.

exercises.prompt: 'Ich stelle das Glas auf _____ Tisch.' (I PUT the glass — motion):
exercises.meaning: Ich stelle das Glas auf den Tisch
exercises.explanation: stellen is a motion verb: the glass travels. wohin? → accusative.

exercises.prompt: 'Das Glas steht auf _____ Tisch.' (The glass STANDS — at rest):
exercises.meaning: Das Glas steht auf dem Tisch
exercises.explanation: stehen is a rest verb: nothing moves. wo? → dative.

exercises.prompt: Match each full sentence with its case logic. Then recall earlier vocabulary in the short phrases:

matching_pairs.english: The cat jumps onto the table
matching_pairs.german: Die Katze springt auf den Tisch

matching_pairs.english: The cat sleeps on the sofa
matching_pairs.german: Die Katze schläft auf dem Sofa

exercises.target_answer: Wir fahren in die Stadt, Wir sind in der Stadt, Die Katze springt auf den Tisch, Die Katze schläft auf dem Sofa, hinter der Tür, neben der Kirche, zwischen Haus und Garten
exercises.meaning: We drive INTO the city (motion); We are in the city (rest); The cat jumps onto the table; The cat sleeps on the sofa; behind the door; beside the church; between house and garden
exercises.explanation: fahren/springt move (accusative); sind/schläft rest (dative) — the verb tells, the case obeys.

exercises.prompt: Cross it: 'Wir gehen über _____ Straße.' (across the street — motion):
exercises.explanation: gehen + über = crossing motion → accusative (die Straße). The hovering bird's über dem Haus was dative.

exercises.prompt: Assemble the German sentence for 'I put the glass under the table':
exercises.target_answer: Ich stelle das Glas unter den Tisch
exercises.meaning: I put the glass under the table
exercises.explanation: stellen (motion) + unter + den (accusative) — the glass travels to its hiding place. Rest would be unter dem Tisch.

summary.outcome: Switch cases by motion vs location in full sentences at speed.

use_example.german: Ich stelle das Glas unter den Tisch.
use_example.english: I put the glass under the table.

summary.takeaway: The verb is the tell: motion verbs drag accusative, rest verbs sit in dative — twenty reps make it reflex.
summary.curiosity_teaser: The drill isle ends here — next branch: first introductions, the first words Germans actually speak.

twist.prompt: Without looking back — build in German: "Today that is very good"
twist.explanation: Building "Heute ist das sehr gut" from the lesson's core pattern locks in Wechselpräpositionen Sentence Gym.

in.etymology_derivation: The identical twin of in (Proto-Germanic *in); two-way preposition: motion → accusative, location → dative. [wiktionary]

auf.context_phrase: Das Buch ist auf dem Tisch.
auf.context_translation: The book is on the table.
auf.etymology_derivation: The twin of up/on (Proto-Germanic *ufa) — and the separable-prefix particle auf = up. [wiktionary]

über.context_translation: We are speaking about / over the book.

unter.context_phrase: Die Katze ist unter dem Tisch.
unter.context_translation: The cat is under the table.
unter.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *undar — the exact twin of under; governs dative (location) and accusative (motion). [wiktionary]

vor.context_phrase: Das Auto steht vor dem Haus.
vor.context_translation: The car stands in front of the house.
vor.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *furai — the twin of English fore (before, forefather); governs dative and accusative. [wiktionary]

hinter.context_phrase: Das Auto ist hinter dem Haus.
hinter.context_translation: The car is behind the house.
hinter.etymology_derivation: The twin of hind (as in hinder, behind) — *hinterą. Two-way preposition. [wiktionary]

neben.context_phrase: Die Katze schläft neben dem Sofa.
neben.context_translation: The cat sleeps beside the sofa.
neben.etymology_derivation: From the *nahuną 'near' family — kin to English nigh. Two-way preposition. [wiktionary]

tisch.context_phrase: Der Teller steht auf dem Tisch.
tisch.context_translation: The plate stands on the table.
tisch.etymology_derivation: Latin discus → Old English disc (dish/desk) → Old High German tisc (tisch, with d → t).

haus.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *hūsą — an exact twin of English house, down to the diphthong. [wiktionary]

neugierig.etymology_derivation: A Middle Low German formation of neu 'new' + gierig 'greedy' — greedy for the new; Dutch nieuwsgierig and Norwegian nysgjerrig are built the same way. [wiktionary]

bart.context_translation: My father wears a full beard.
bart.etymology_derivation: From Old High German bart, from Proto-Germanic *bardaz, from PIE *bʰardʰéh₂. English beard is a listed cognate. [wiktionary]

retten.etymology_derivation: From Proto-Germanic *hradjaną (to save); the page names English redd (dialectal, to put right) and everyday rid as cognates — to rid someone of danger is to rescue them. [wiktionary]

klinik.etymology_derivation: A 19th-century learned word from Greek kline, bed (klinike techne, the bedside art) — the same Greek source as English clinic. [wiktionary]
